findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-QIAN-23.result.json: items 087 and 088 (statements and proof outlines), item 135's application, source issue E43, routes 1 and 4
findings.claim: The accepted E43 correction is not implemented in the theorem contracts. Items 087–088 still identify consecutive Hodge–Tate weights starting at λ_τ with automorphic weight −λ_τ and still assert central-character valuation −nλ_τ and partial valuation −jλ_τ. In the fixed conventions these signs are positive. Item 135 must use a consistently renamed parameter when applied to those items.
findings.evidence: Published Qian, proof of Lemma 4.3 p.1273, contains the printed sign error that E43 already confirms. ACC+, journal pp.906–908, fixes geometric Artin and HT(ε)={−1}; p.987 gives HT_τ(r_ι(ω_π))=Σ_i λ_{τ,i}, and Theorem 6.1.1(5)(b), p.1029, gives HT_τ(r_ι(π))={λ_{τ,1}+n−1,…,λ_{τ,n}}. Thus consecutive weights beginning at λ_τ correspond to constant weight +λ_τ. For a Hecke character φ with Galois weights h_τ, r_ι(φ)∘Art_v=ι⁻¹φ_v·∏_τ τ(·)^(−h_τ); the left side has unit values, giving valuation +Σ_τ h_τ val_l(τ(ϖ_v)). The norm character, with Galois realization ε and h_τ=−1, has local value q_v⁻¹, immediately detecting the sign. Applying this to the central character gives +nλ_τ and hence +jλ_τ. E43 states exactly this repair, but the operative items retain the opposite formulas.
findings.fix: Propagate the existing E43 correction into the current statements and proof outlines of 087–088 and their routed ordinary-automorphy use. Coordinate item 135's parameter with the same weight convention (or explicitly rename its dual parameter before substitution). Check the corrected central and j-th slope formulas against the norm character and a nonzero Tate twist. Preserve the valid conclusion of Lemma 4.3 and the existing semisimplicity qualification; this finding concerns an unpropagated correction, not a new objection to the main theorem.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-QIAN-23.result.json: item 076 hypothesis and conclusion (iv), item 078 hypothesis/application of item 014; route 13
findings.claim: Containing one m-th root of each element of F_(l^s) does not imply containing μ_m. Item 076(iv) is false under its stated hypothesis, and item 078 invokes the root-character lemma without establishing its roots-of-unity hypothesis.
findings.evidence: Published §4 opening, p.1268, requires the coefficient field generated by “all the m-th roots”, whereas 076 and 078 require only an m-th root of each element. Set l=3, n=m=7, s=1, N=7381=11²·61 and F=Q(i), with trivial residual representation. N is odd, coprime to ln and greater than 100n+100. The order of 3 modulo N is 10, so any residue field at 3 of Q(ζ_N) is k=F_(3^10), which contains F_9. Since gcd(7,3^10−1)=gcd(7,59048)=1, seventh powering is an automorphism of k×: in particular every element of F_3 has a seventh root in k. But 7 does not divide 59048, so μ_7 is not contained in k. Thus 076(iv) fails. The extra exclusion N∤3^(10/2)+1 used in 078 also holds (the latter integer is 244). Item 073 and route 13's stronger all-roots instruction already avoid this problem.
findings.fix: Require all m-th roots of every element of F_(l^s) in both 076 and 078, as in the source and route 13, or add μ_m⊂k explicitly alongside the existing existential root condition. Recheck the call to 014 and the coefficient-field construction using those exact hypotheses. Add the displayed finite-field example as a negative specification for the weaker condition. Keep E5's valid correction m | #k× when n=l^a m; this is a separate quantifier error.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-QIAN-23.result.json: item 139's sufficient-condition clause, item 105.note, route 13's general-character companion branch
findings.claim: The claim that occurrence of 0 among the Dwork exponents implies maximal unipotent monodromy at infinity is false. Item 139 imports it from the companion's Remark 1.2, and item 105 repeats it as an alternative justification.
findings.evidence: Companion arXiv:2103.00106v1, p.2 Remark 1.2, states the zero-exponent shortcut. Take N=5 and a=(1,2,2,0,0), whose sum is 0 modulo 5. A'Campo arXiv:2407.16481v1, Definitions 2.1.1–2.1.2 (pp.7–8), identifies this character, up to permutation, with α=(0,3), β=(1,2) modulo 5: −α=(0,2), and the complement of −β is {0,1,2}. Proposition 2.1.3 gives rank two. Proposition 2.5.7 (pp.19–20; also 2.1.4 p.8) gives infinity Jordan-block sizes equal to the multiplicities of α. Here they are 1 and 1, so monodromy is the identity with minimal polynomial X−1, not (X−1)². All coefficient conjugates retain distinct α values. Reversing the cohomological action convention only dualizes this identity operator. This is also consistent with invariance of the H_0-character under simultaneous translation of all exponents: mere occurrence of zero cannot be an intrinsic criterion.
findings.fix: Remove the zero-exponent sufficient condition from 139 and 105's note and record a source issue for Remark 1.2. Retain the actual maximal-monodromy hypothesis in the general companion theorem, together with its already recorded Hodge–Tate gap. For Qian's selected family use the separately proved Corollary 3.5 (item 049) and coefficient-conjugation compatibility. If an exponent criterion is wanted, derive it from the actual Jordan-block multiplicities and prove its applicability; do not infer it from one exponent being zero. Add the rank-two example as a negative specification. This does not refute the companion's conditional theorem or the published potential-automorphy results.
